bib.title: Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models

SOURCE: "Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models" (DreamerV3), Danijar Hafner, Jurgis Pasukonis, Jimmy Ba, Timothy Lillicrap (Google DeepMind; University of Toronto). Preprint.
- Version: the p1 stamp reads "arXiv:2301.04104v2 [cs.AI] 17 Apr 2024", so this is v2, not v1. PDF metadata creation date is 2024-04-18. The repo filename says 2023.
- Venue: the PDF names no journal or conference. Confirm any venue outside this file. I did not fill it from memory.

COVERAGE: 85,073 of 85,073 chars; 40 of 40 pages. That covers Methods (pp17-22), Supplementary (pp23-40) and all results tables. References were skimmed for origins. Figures were read from captions only; images were not inspected.

CLAIMS
- claim: One configuration beats specialised methods across 8 domains.
  number: over 150 tasks; 8 domains
  setup: Atari, ProcGen, DMLab, Minecraft, Atari100k, Proprio Control, Visual Control, BSuite. Table 4 values are fixed, but see the first LIMITS item: model size and replay ratio vary.
  quote: "We evaluate the generality of Dreamer across 8 domains—with over 150 tasks—under fixed hyper-parameters." / "The same values are used across all benchmarks, including proprioceptive and visual inputs, continuous and discrete actions, and 2D and 3D domains."
  where: p8; p21 Table 4
- claim: Every Dreamer run on Minecraft found a diamond within budget, from scratch; no baseline did.
  number: 100% vs 0% of agents; 100M env steps; 10 seeds
  setup: sparse +1 for 12 milestones, each once per episode; episodes up to 36000 steps; baselines PPO, and IMPALA and Rainbow tuned by the authors.
  quote: "over the course of training, 100% of Dreamer agents obtain one or more diamonds regardless of episode boundaries, compared to 0% of the baseline agents."
  where: p24 Fig 9; seeds p19
- claim: Per episode, diamonds remain rare, and the authors say so.
  number: 0.4% of episodes
  setup: at the 100M step budget.
  quote: "At the budget, Dreamer obtains diamonds in 0.4% of episodes, leaving a challenge for future research."
  where: p24
- claim: Minecraft final return is highest for Dreamer.
  number: 9.1 vs IMPALA 7.1, Rainbow 6.3, PPO 5.1
  setup: 100M env steps, Table 5.
  quote: "Dreamer 9.1 / IMPALA 7.1 / Rainbow 6.3 / PPO 5.1" (table rows)
  where: p24
- claim: Compute is far lower than VPT's, though VPT is a different setup (behavioural cloning plus RL finetuning).
  number: 1 GPU for 9 days vs 720 GPUs for 9 days
  setup: Table 2 lists 8.9 GPU days for Minecraft.
  quote: "using 720 GPUs for 9 days. In comparison, Dreamer uses the MineRL competition action space to autonomously learn to collect diamonds from sparse rewards using 1 GPU for 9 days, without human data."
  where: p11
- claim: Atari: slightly ahead of MuZero, well ahead of PPO.
  number: gamer median 830% vs MuZero 693%, PPO 180%; gamer mean 3381 vs 3054 vs 892; record mean capped 38 vs 34 vs 21
  setup: 57 games, 200M steps, sticky actions.
  quote: "Gamer median (%) 0 100 3716 180 693 830"
  where: p26 Table 6
- claim: ProcGen: a tie with PPG rather than a clear win.
  number: 66.01 vs PPG 64.89, PPO 42.80, original PPO 41.16
  setup: 16 games, 50M steps, hard mode, 1 seed.
  quote: "Normalized mean 41.16 42.80 64.89 66.01"; text says "matches the tuned expert algorithm PPG"
  where: p28 Table 7; p8
- claim: DMLab: beats baselines given 10x the data, but not the 10B-step scores.
  number: human mean capped 71.4 at 100M; IMPALA 66.3 at 1B, 85.1 at 10B; R2D2+ 85.4 at 10B; PPO 35.9 and IMPALA 31.0 at 100M
  setup: 30 tasks.
  quote: "amounting to a data-efficiency gain of over 1000%. We note that these baselines were not designed for data-efficiency"; "Human mean capped (%) 85.4 85.1 66.3 31.0 35.9 71.4"
  where: p8; p30 Table 8
- claim: Atari100k: leads on mean among comparable protocols, but not on median and not over EfficientMuZero.
  number: gamer mean 125 vs IRIS 105, TWM 96; median 49 vs TWM 51; EffMuZero 190 / 109
  setup: 26 games, 400K env steps. Table 10 notes protocol differences (planning, early resets, resolution).
  quote: "Gamer score (%) 33 190 62 105 96 125" / "Gamer median (%) 13 109 40 29 51 49"
  where: p32 Tables 9-10
- claim: Control suites: new state of the art on task mean.
  number: Proprio 871 vs DMPO 801, D4PG 792, PPO 94 (500K steps, 18 tasks). Visual 861 vs DrQ-v2 770, CURL 479, PPO 94 (1M steps, 20 tasks)
  setup: action repeat 2; both use the 12M model.
  quote: "Task mean 94 771 801 792 871"; "Task mean 94 81 479 770 861"
  where: p34; p36
- claim: BSuite: best overall and on scale and memory, but near zero on exploration.
  number: task mean 66 vs Boot DQN 60; scale 0.82 vs 0.60; exploration 0.01 vs Boot DQN 0.68
  setup: 23 environments, 468 configurations, 10 seeds.
  quote: "Task mean (%) 3 49 32 54 60 66"; "Exploration 0.00 0.00 0.00 0.00 0.68 0.01"
  where: p10; p38 Table 13
- claim: Replay ratio is the compute-versus-data dial: higher ratios predictably raise performance and lower the data needed.
  number: replay ratio 32 with action repeat 4 and batch 16 × 64 gives 1 gradient step per 128 env steps, 1.5M updates over 200M steps; ratios used range 32 to 1024
  setup: scaling results from Crafter and one DMLab task only, read from Fig 6 curves; no numeric table.
  quote: "a replay ratio of 32 on Atari with action repeat of 4 and batch shape 16 × 64 corresponds to 1 gradient step every 128 env steps, or 1.5M gradient steps over 200M env steps."
  where: p18; p9-10; p19 Table 2
- claim: Bigger models score higher and need less environment interaction.
  number: 12M to 400M parameters, 6 sizes
  setup: same Crafter and DMLab experiment; all hyperparameters fixed across sizes.
  quote: "we train 6 model sizes ranging from 12M to 400M parameters" / "increasing the model size directly translates to both higher task performance and a lower data requirement."
  where: p10; p20
- claim: All robustness techniques help on average; each is critical only on some tasks. The KL objective matters most, then return normalisation and symexp twohot.
  number: 14 tasks
  setup: curves only (Fig 6a, Fig 17); no numeric effect sizes in the text.
  quote: "we ablate the robustness techniques and learning signals on a diverse set of 14 tasks" / "each individual technique is critical on a subset of tasks but may not affect performance on other tasks."
  where: p10
- claim: Performance rests mainly on the unsupervised reconstruction signal, not on reward and value gradients.
  number: none
  setup: 14 tasks, gradient-stopping ablation.
  quote: "Dreamer rests predominantly on the unsupervised objective of its world model."
  where: p10

MECHANISMS (explicitly requested)
- Symlog: predict symlog(y), read out with symexp. Used on vector observations (encoder inputs and decoder targets). It avoids large-target divergence, truncation and normalisation non-stationarity. "symlog transformations avoid truncating large targets, introducing non-stationary from normalization, or adjusting network weights when new extreme values are detected" (p7, citation digits stripped).
- Symexp two-hot: reward predictor and critic output a softmax over symexp(−20...+20) bins, trained by cross entropy on two-hot targets, "decoupling the size of the gradients from the size of the targets" (p7).
- Percentile return normalisation: fixed entropy scale 3×10⁻⁴. Returns are divided by max(1, S), where S is an EMA (0.99) of the 95th minus 5th percentile, so "we only scale down large return magnitudes but leave small returns below the threshold of L = 1 untouched" (p6). Authors "did not find stable hyperparameters across domains" for advantage normalisation, standard-deviation normalisation or constrained entropy (p6).
- KL balance and free bits: βdyn = 1, βrep = 0.1, losses clipped below 1 nat. "combining free bits with a small representation loss resolves this dilemma, allowing for fixed hyperparameters across domains" (p5). 1% uniform mix on categoricals (p5, p18).
- RSSM (p3-4, p18): sequence model ht = f(ht−1, zt−1, at−1) is a block GRU with 8 blocks. Encoder zt ~ q(zt | ht, xt); dynamics predictor ẑt ~ p(ẑt | ht); reward, continue and decoder heads read from (ht, zt). Latents are vectors of softmax categoricals with straight-through gradients. CNNs handle images, MLPs handle vectors.
- Imagined rollouts (p5-6): the actor and critic "learn behaviors purely from abstract trajectories of representations predicted by the world model." Rollouts start from replayed representations, horizon T = 16 in the text. The critic learns the distribution of bootstrapped λ-returns (λ = 0.95, γ = 0.997), plus a replay-trajectory critic loss at scale 0.3, and is regularised towards an EMA copy (decay 0.98). The actor uses Reinforce for both discrete and continuous actions. In the environment: "sampling from the actor network without lookahead planning."
- Other fixed values (p21): LaProp, learning rate 4×10⁻⁵, AGC(0.3), batch 16 × 64, replay capacity 5×10⁶, uniform replay with an online queue.

LIMITS
Conceded by the authors, or visible in the tables:
- "Fixed hyperparameters" covers Table 4, not everything. Table 2 varies model size (200M, but 12M on both control suites), replay ratio (32 to 1024, "chosen to fit the step budget of each benchmark"), action repeat and env instances. A course note should not say "nothing changes per domain".
- Minecraft is an author-modified setup, and its protocol is self-established. They remove early termination on diamond ore, hold jump for 200ms, follow the "block breaking setting of prior work", use a flat categorical action space and abstract crafting actions, and add ±0.01 heart rewards ("did not investigate whether this is helpful"). "we establish the evaluation protocol" (p19). So "from scratch" means no human data or curricula, not raw default MineRL.
- "First" has a qualifier in the paper: Voyager reaches similar technology-tree depth via LLM API calls on a scripted layer (p11). VPT obtains diamonds with human data.
- Seeds: 5 per benchmark, but "1 seed for ProcGen due to computational constraints" (p19). Curves show mean ± 1 std; no significance tests appear.
- PPO was tuned by the authors (Acme implementation, discount matched to Dreamer). They validate it against ProcGen only. Other baselines are literature numbers, with protocol differences on Atari100k and a 10x data allowance on DMLab.
- Uniform replay was chosen for ease even though prioritised replay "improve[s] the performance of Dreamer" (p18), so results are not maximal.
- Weak tasks in the tables: Deep Sea 0.00; Venture 0; Pitfall 0; Skiing −29965, which is below the random score of −17098; Montezuma 1852 vs gamer 4753; Bigfish 8.62 vs PPG 31.26; Freeway at Atari100k 0.
- Authors' bottom-line limit: 0.4% per-episode diamonds, "leaving a challenge for future research."

Not shown (my reading; the paper does not state these):
- No real-robot or other real-world experiment. All domains are simulated or games, and "practical applications" is an aspiration.
- No single world model across domains; that is named as future work (p11).
- No unsupervised pretraining; "could allow for future algorithm variants" (p10).
- No hyperparameter-sensitivity sweep for Table 4 values.
- No numeric table for ablations or scaling; replay and size scaling rest on 2 tasks.
- No claim about optimality, or about wins on every task.

CODE: The PDF has no code, only equations. It says a public implementation is "available on the project website" but prints no URL.
- p7 Eq 9, verbatim extraction, parentheses lost: "symlog(x) .= sign(x) ln |x| + 1 symexp(x) .= sign(x) exp(|x|) − 1". Check the rendered page before copying.
- p7 Eq 8: "L(θ) .= 12  f (x, θ) − symlog(y)2 ˆy .= symexp f (x, θ)".
- p6 Eq 7: "S .= EMA  Per(Rλt , 95) − Per(Rλt , 5), 0.99".

FIGURES:
- Fig 3, p3: "Training process of Dreamer" shows world-model learning beside actor-critic learning in imagination. This is the best single explainer of the architecture.
- Fig 1, p1: benchmark bars ("Tuned experts / Unified configuration") plus the Minecraft curve; gives the generality claim at a glance.
- Fig 6, p9: ablations plus model-size and replay scaling; shows the compute-versus-data trade-off.
- Fig 5, p8: fraction of agents reaching iron ingot, iron pickaxe and diamond. Pair it with Fig 9.
- Fig 9, p24: per-episode item rates. It contrasts 100% of agents with 0.4% of episodes, which guards against misreading Fig 5.
- Fig 4, p4: 5 context frames, then 45 open-loop predicted frames; makes "imagination" concrete.

PROBLEMS:
- Extraction: displayed equations lose brackets and subscripts; superscript citations fuse with text. Figure bar values are not extractable, so numbers above come from tables only.
- Internal inconsistencies in the source:
  - Imagination horizon is T = 16 on p5 but H = 15 in Table 4.
  - Table 3 prints 1024 recurrent units for 12M, whereas 8d with d = 256 would be 2048.
  - p8 says IMPALA and R2D2+ at 1B, but Table 8 labels its only R2D2+ column 10B (85.4). Fig 1 labels R2D2+ "10x data".
  - Table 2's task counts sum to 191 (my arithmetic), consistent with "over 150".
  - Typos in the source: "synexp", "comntains", "world world".
- No embedded instructions found.
